original_test_intent: Read BMC DNS server configuration from Redfish and verify its description/values match the platform specification.
original_method: Resolve the Manager NetworkProtocol resource from advertised links, read the complete DNS configuration securely and compare schema-valid NameServers to approved expected values using documented address and ordering rules.
manual_activity: Provide the target Manager/NetworkProtocol schema, expected DNS server set/order and approved rules for IPv4, IPv6, hostname and sensitive-address comparison.
required_inputs: Exact Manager and NetworkProtocol advertised links
safety_requirements: Do not assume ManagerId `bmc` without discovery
No hardcoded credentials or TLS bypass
Capture complete response before field projection
Never resolve hostnames as a substitute for configured-string comparison unless the spec requires it
Redact management topology in stored evidence
agent_execution_scope: Use secret-backed read-only authentication over verified TLS
Capture HTTP status and complete JSON
Compare count, order and values as required
Emit exact missing/mismatch reasons with redacted display
engineer_actions: Provide endpoint/schema and expected DNS values

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It identifies a plausible DNS field, but hardcodes `/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol`, bypasses TLS, returns only NameServers and cannot satisfy the external-spec criterion without values and list semantics.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Follow the advertised NetworkProtocol link, securely capture the complete document, validate NameServers against the target schema and compare raw/canonical values to the approved DNS specification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The DNS scope and 15/10 timing remain; ManagerId, expected addresses, order, address family and normalization are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform a provenance-bound, lossless comparison of the configured DNS list, including cardinality, order when meaningful, address-family normalization and explicit redaction.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces the placeholder and unsupported YES with endpoint discovery, a supplied oracle, schema validation and deterministic list comparison.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates configured NameServers only; it does not test resolver reachability, lookup latency, search domains, failover or DNSSEC.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A configuration match can coexist with unreachable servers, while hostname resolution during comparison can introduce changing external state and must not be assumed.

project_override_considerations: If the target exposes DNS configuration through an EthernetInterface or OEM property rather than ManagerNetworkProtocol, use the approved schema and retain the variance. An empty list is evaluated only against the platform policy, not automatically failed.
expected_evidence: DNS specification revision and expected values
HTTP status and complete response hash
Raw and canonicalized configured server list
No DNS/network mutation and preserved logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Criteria consistently identify a DNS-versus-spec read-only check. The Procedure is a placeholder and lacks implementation detail, but it does not assert a competing target or operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The real endpoint/schema, expected DNS values and comparison rules are identifiable package inputs, so the case is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Reclassifies an unverifiable placeholder and one-field dump into a target-discovered, specification-backed DNS configuration comparison with explicit address semantics and privacy controls.
independent_technical_reasoning: DNS configuration is a list whose semantics may include priority/order, multiple address families and empty secondary slots. Text equality can misclassify equivalent IPv6 forms, while set equality can conceal an incorrect primary/secondary order, so the specification must decide comparison behavior. The Manager NetworkProtocol URI also must be discovered because implementations vary. This case proves configured values only; resolver function would need a controlled query and per-server/failover evidence under a separate test.
